Reduce a pedigree to the near relatives of a group

Source: R/getNearRelativePedigree.R
getNearRelativePedigree.Rd

Keeps each animal within a distance of the probands, and the parents that join those animals' families, as Pedixplorer's useful_inds() does when given max_dist.

Usage

getNearRelativePedigree(ped, probands, maxDist)

Arguments

ped

a data frame with the columns id, sire and dam (an unknown parent is NA). Factor columns are read by their labels and numbers as text.

probands

a vector of the animals whose near relatives are kept, compared with id as text. An id with no row is ignored.

maxDist

one finite number, 1 or more: the largest distance kept.

Value

ped with only the rows kept, in their order and with their row names, each column and its type unchanged, and NA for each sire or dam left out; no rows when no proband has a row.

Details

An animal's distance is log2(1 / k), where k is its largest kinship (kinship) with a proband: 1 for a proband itself, 2 for a parent, offspring or full sibling, 3 for a grandparent, grandoffspring, half sibling, uncle, aunt, nephew or niece, 4 for a first cousin, and so on. Distance is read from kinship, not counted in steps, so a double first cousin is at 3 and an inbred animal can be at less than 1; an animal not related to any proband has no distance and is kept only as a parent.

Every animal within maxDist is kept. So is each parent of a kept animal whose own offspring and the offspring of its mates (with any partner), counted once, number two or more; any other parent is left out, and its id is set to NA in its offspring's row, as removeAnimals does. On the pedigrees its tests compare, the animals kept are the ones Pedixplorer 1.8.0's useful_inds(max_dist = maxDist) marks useful, with the same informative animals.

Pedixplorer chooses its informative animals with is_informative(), by default those both available and affected; pass those as probands, for instance ped$id[genotyped & ped$affected].

A pedigree from which kinship cannot be read is refused: getNearRelativePedigree() stops, naming the animals, when checkPedigree reports missingIds, duplicateIds, ownParent, cycle, rowlessParents (addParents adds a row for each such parent) or missingParentCodes. Sex is not read, and one known parent is legal.

See also

getProbandPedigree, getDescendantPedigree, trimPedigree, removeAnimals, kinship

Examples

## O is the proband. F and M are its parents, S its sister and K its
## offspring by Q. G1 and G2 are F's parents, U is F's brother and C is
## U's offspring by X. S has N by Y and N2 by Z.
ped <- data.frame(
  id = c("G1", "G2", "F", "U", "M", "X", "O", "S", "Q", "K", "Y", "Z",
         "N", "N2", "C"),
  sire = c(NA, NA, "G1", "G1", NA, NA, "F", "F", NA, "O", NA, NA, "Y",
           "Z", "U"),
  dam = c(NA, NA, "G2", "G2", NA, NA, "M", "M", NA, "Q", NA, NA, "S",
          "S", "X")
)
## Distance 1: O, and its parents F and M, who have two offspring.
near1 <- getNearRelativePedigree(ped, "O", 1)
near1$id
#> [1] "F" "M" "O"
## Distance 2: also S, K, G1 and G2. Q is left out (K is its only
## offspring and O has no other), so K's dam is NA.
near2 <- getNearRelativePedigree(ped, "O", 2)
near2[near2$id == "K", ]
#>    id sire  dam
#> 10  K    O <NA>
## Distance 3: also U, N and N2, and their sires Y and Z, each with one
## offspring by S, who has two.
near3 <- getNearRelativePedigree(ped, "O", 3)
near3$id
#>  [1] "G1" "G2" "F"  "U"  "M"  "O"  "S"  "K"  "Y"  "Z"  "N"  "N2"
